newsitem.title: UK: Eurobonds quiet amid widespread European holiday.
newsitem.headline: Eurobonds quiet amid widespread European holiday.

text.p: Primary market activity was at a standstill on Monday morning with most centres on continental Europe closed for a holiday.
The meeting of the policy-making U.S. Federal Open Market Committee on Tuesday means the delayed start to the week will likely be extended, dealers said.
Among limited related activity, Daily Mail and General Trust Plc offered to buy back the 48 million stg outstanding on its 5.75 percent 2003 bond exchangeable into Reuters shares.
Daily Mail will issue a new bond due 2004 which will be exchangeable into Reuters shares.
J.P. Morgan Securities will arrange/lead manage the two separate Daily Mail transactions.
The repurchase price of the 2003 bonds will be at an indicated 6-8 percent premium over the market price.
The outstanding bond was issued in September 1993 at an exchange price of 4.795 stg per share. At 1000 GMT Reuters was quoted at 666 pence stg, down 6p on the day.
Deals scheduled for later this week included Pakistan's well-flagged dollar FRN, seen as $200 million at around 400 basis points over LIBOR. ANZ Investment Bank is lead manager.
